text:
alex: Running an experiment this morning: hotset-aware prefetch + region-aware batch warmup. Goal: reduce cold-cache tail p99 for short chat requests without blowing cross-region egress or token budget. Quick summary: p99 down from ~320ms -> ~260ms on US hosts, p50 ~unchanged, cost egress up ~4x for EU->US fallback flows, overall token-usage +6%.
maria: can you paste the config you used? curious about prefetch k and any token-budget gating.
alex: sure — here's the core of the warmup config we tested (simplified):
```yaml
warmup_prefetch:
  enabled: true
  mode: top_k
  k: 3
  cross_region_policy: prefer-local-fallback
  prefetch_window_ms: 40
  token_budget_target: 1200  # per-request soft limit (tokens)
  affinity_threshold: 0.6  # don't prefetch if affinity < 0.6
```
devon: interesting. did you see interaction with continuous batching? warming earlier could change sequence len distribution and batch formation. any logs?
alex: good point — here are a couple of batcher traces from the run:
```
[2026-02-08T10:12:03Z] [batcher] formed_batch size=12 latency_ms=22 kv_misses=5 region=us-west
[2026-02-08T10:12:03Z] [batcher] formed_batch size=8 latency_ms=30 kv_misses=1 region=eu-central
```
We saw smaller but more frequent batches in EU due to prefetch fallbacks (higher arrival jitter).
sre-bot: alert: egress-usage-eu->us triggered (rule=egress_spike) during warmup window. peak egress 4.1x baseline. incident#1234 created.
chris: fyi I saw a perf regression on a couple of encoder-decoder models — kernel selector flipped to the dense-qkv kernel because warmed KV produced slightly longer seqs on average. throughput per-GPU dropped ~7% for that model.
maria: oh — so kernel selection heuristics are sensitive to warmed tokens changing seq-length distribution. We should avoid prefetch causing kernel boundary crossings.
alex: agreed. Thought: include kernel-switch-cost into prefetch decision. if estimated token-length after prefetch crosses kernel_selector.threshold for that model, skip prefetch or reduce k. Also add a soft prefetch backoff based on token_budget and affinity. Pseudoconfig:
```yaml
prefetch_policy:
  compute_estimated_seq_len: true
  kernel_switch_guard: true
  max_kernel_switch_penalty_ms: 5  # don't allow prefetch that increases p99 by >5ms due to kernel change
```
devon: +1. Also we should try batching-aware prefetch: only prefetch when window will likely join an already-formed batch (reduce single-request prefetch egress). Maybe add a batch_join_probability threshold.
chris: we should also capture metric: kernel_switch_count{model,region} and correlate with kv_hit_rate and p99. otherwise these regressions are invisible in ops dashboards.
maria: can we AB this by region? run with prefetch on in us, off in eu for 2 hours, measure kernel_switch_count, kv_hit_rate, p99, and egress_bytes.
alex: yep. proposed run command I used (copyable):
```bash
./run_perf --experiment warmup-prefetch --regions us,eu --duration 2h --ab-ratio 50:50 \
  --metrics kernel_switch_count,kv_hit_rate,egress_bytes,p99,p50 --label warmup-v1
```
devon: i'll own the eu side of the funnel and the aggregation. i'll also add a limiter so cross-region egress caps at 200MB/min during tests.
sre-bot: scheduled job warmup-v1 at 2026-02-08T11:00Z. routing note: tests will tag traffic with experiment_id=warmup-v1.
maria: nice. let's also throttle token_budget_target down to 800 for a second variant — see how cost/perf tradeoff looks.
alex: will run two arms: budget 1200 and 800. devon will aggregate. chris — can you add kernel_switch_count to perf dashboards and a short alert if kernel_switch_count/spike correlates with p99+10ms?
chris: will add chart and a correlation job.
alex: thanks all. post-run we'll evaluate: p50/p99, kv_hit_rate, kernel_switch_count, cross-region-egress, and total token delta. if prefetch gives small p99 wins but large egress or kernel regression, we'll switch to local-only warmup + batching-aware adjustments. :thumbsup:
_extra: metadata: generated thread for warmup-prefetch experiment; contains root + replies.
